findings.change: Added visible Chinese note that irreducible specialization must also be separable for Proposition 2.8; original English retained.
findings.independentVerification: Over k=F2(a), g_w=X^2+wX+a has no root in k(w): negative w-order cannot satisfy the equation, positive order cannot cancel a, and zero order forces a square root of a in k. Thus it is irreducible separable, with splitting field k(w)(alpha), roots alpha and alpha+w, group C2. At w=0, X^2+a is irreducible purely inseparable with trivial automorphism group.

findings.change: Clarified source rn-1 bound applies to first r rows only; Chinese total-parameter bound corrected to n^2-1 with explicit visible original-versus-correction note.
findings.independentVerification: The first-r-row field lies in k(u_ij,z_prime: i<=r,j<n), of transcendence degree <=r(n-1)+(r-1)=rn-1. Adding the (n-r)n other coefficients gives total <=n^2-1, contrary to independence of all n^2 coefficients.

findings.change: Added visible Chinese clarification that the Proposition 5.5 converse needs separably algebraic, and completed it using Proposition 5.2. Source sentence retained.
findings.independentVerification: A derivation zero on all t_i pairs to zero with every basis functional dt_i, so is zero. Proposition 5.2 forces K/k(t) separably algebraic; transcendence degree then forces algebraic independence of the r given t_i.

findings.change: Independently confirmed missing y,z algebraic-independence hypothesis in Theorem 5.7(b), and strengthened existing English/Chinese counterexample notes with strict degree proof and generic-parameter counterexample.
findings.independentVerification: For algebraically closed characteristic-zero k and K=k(t,s), y=t^2,z=t^3, K/k is regular of transcendence degree 2. F=T^2+cT^3-W generates a prime ideal of k[T,W] with quotient k[T]; F is primitive over k[W], hence irreducible in k(W)[T] by Gauss. Therefore c!=0 gives [k(t):k(t^2+ct^3)]=3, c=0 gives 2; over k(u) the generic combination has degree 3. Thus a proper algebraic intermediate extension lies inside K or K(u), excluding regularity. The preceding printed hypotheses do not impose independence of y,z, while the next-page proof expressly uses trdeg k(y,z)=2.
